new.name: Zug Bug
new.description: A classic peacock nymph: peacock sword tail, peacock herl body ribbed with oval silver, a brown hackle beard and a short clipped mallard wing case.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift or swing it; a great general nymph for trout and panfish.
steps: Tie in a short peacock sword tail and the tinsel.
Wind a full peacock herl body and rib it.
Tie a brown hackle beard underneath.
Tie a mallard flank wing case on top, trim it to a third of the body, whip finish.
new.imitates: Caddis larvae and mayfly nymphs; a general nymph

new.name: Three Dollar Dip
new.description: A simple brown thread pupa with a gold rib, a gold bead and a little bleached elk hair wing bud.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it small under an indicator on tailwaters during midge and Baetis activity.
steps: Add the bead, tie in the wire and wrap a slim brown thread body.
Rib it in even turns.
Tie in a few bleached elk hairs on top behind the bead, trim them short as wing buds.
Whip finish.

new.name: Iris Caddis
new.description: A caddis emerger: a Z-Lon trailing shuck, a slim dubbed body and a loop wing of Z-Lon over a dubbed head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film during evening caddis hatches.
steps: Tie in a short Z-Lon shuck.
Dub a slim body to two-thirds of the shank.
Tie in a Z-Lon loop on top as the wing.
Dub a rough head and whip finish.

new.name: CDC Midge Pupa
new.description: A thread-bodied midge pupa ribbed with wire, with a little CDC puff at the head to hold it in the film.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in or just under the film during midge hatches.
steps: Wrap a slim ribbed thread body.
Tie in a small CDC puff on top.
Wrap a small thorax and whip finish.

new.name: Fat Albert
new.description: A two-layer foam hopper/stonefly with a sparkle wing, rubber legs and a bright indicator.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a high-floating dry-dropper indicator in summer.
steps: Tie a foam strip down along the shank in segments.
Add the wing on top at the front segment.
Tie in rubber legs each side and the indicator.
Whip finish.

new.name: CDC & Elk
new.description: A wound CDC feather body with an elk hair wing whose butts form the head. Simple and very effective.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to caddis-feeding trout in riffles and runs.
steps: Tie in a CDC feather by its tip at the bend.
Wind it forward, stroking the fibres back.
Tie in an elk hair wing, trim the butts square as a head.
Whip finish behind the head.

new.name: Hoh Bo Spey
new.description: A shank-style steelhead spey fly: pink butt, purple Ice Dub body over a pink guinea rib support, black marabou and fuchsia flash collar, with a pink Amherst front collar.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for winter steelhead on sink-tips.
mats: Black spey marabou with fuchsia flash
steps: Attach the hook to the shank with a braided loop.
Dub a pink butt and wind a pink guinea feather as a support collar.
Dub a purple body.
Wind black marabou with fuchsia flash, then a pink Amherst collar.
Whip finish.

new.name: Matt's Midge
new.description: A tiny black thread midge with a white Z-Lon wing and a grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to sipping trout during winter midge hatches.
steps: Wrap a slim black thread body.
Tie in a short white wing.
Wind two or three turns of grizzly and whip finish.

new.name: Jujubee Midge
new.description: A segmented midge pupa with a two-tone Super Hair abdomen, a white wing bud and a dark thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in tailwaters under an indicator, or high in the column during hatches.
mats: Two strands of Super Hair wrapped together
steps: Tie in the two Super Hair strands and wrap them together for a striped abdomen.
Tie in a white Z-Lon wing bud.
Dub a small thorax, pull the wing over and whip finish.

new.name: Fur Ant
new.description: Two humps of black dubbing with a few turns of hackle at the waist.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film along banks on summer days.
steps: Dub a round rear hump.
Wind two turns of hackle in the middle.
Dub a smaller front hump and whip finish.

new.name: March Brown Dry
new.description: A big Catskill dun: wood duck wings, a ginger tail, tan dubbed body and mixed brown and grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during the late-spring March brown hatch on eastern rivers.
steps: Tie in the wood duck wings, upright and divided.
Add a ginger tail.
Dub a tan body.
Wind the hackles and whip finish.

new.name: Hornberg
new.description: A Wisconsin classic: silver body, yellow hackle-tip underwing, mallard flank wing, jungle cock and a grizzly collar. Fished dry or wet.
new.fishing_tips: Skate it dry, then let it sink and strip it back like a minnow.
steps: Wrap a silver body.
Tie in yellow hackle tips as an underwing.
Fold mallard flank around them as the wing and add cheeks.
Wind a grizzly collar and whip finish.

new.name: Bob's Banger
new.description: A foam cylinder popper that pushes lots of water, with a bucktail and flash tail.
new.fishing_tips: Pop it loudly over striper and bluefish blitzes, or for bass in the weeds.
mats: Foam cylinder slid over the shank
steps: Tie a bucktail and flash tail.
Glue a foam cylinder onto the shank.
Add eyes and let it set.

new.name: Greenwell's Glory
new.creator_name: James Wright for Canon William Greenwell (1854)
new.description: A famous Tweed wet fly: waxed yellow silk body that turns olive, ribbed with gold wire, a furnace hackle and starling wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it in spring when olives hatch.
steps: Wrap a waxed yellow silk body and rib it with gold.
Tie a furnace hackle beard or collar.
Tie in matched wing slips, whip finish.

new.name: No-Hackle Dun
new.description: A hackleless dun with split tails and duck-quill wings, sitting flat in the film like a natural.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to selective trout on spring creeks and flat water.
steps: Tie in the split tails.
Dub a slim body.
Tie a wing slip on each side of the thorax.
Dub around the wings and whip finish.

new.name: Guide's Choice Hare's Ear
new.description: A beaded hare's ear with a pearl flashback, peacock thorax, partridge hackle and a fluorescent orange hot spot.
new.fishing_tips: A searching nymph for any trout stream.
steps: Add the bead and weight.
Tie in a hare's mask tail and the rib; dub the abdomen and rib it.
Tie in the flash, wrap a peacock thorax, pull the flash over.
Wind a partridge collar and finish with an orange thread hot spot.

new.name: AP Nymph
new.description: A buggy, all-purpose nymph: moose or hair tail and wing case, a beaver fur body ribbed with copper.
new.fishing_tips: A general searching nymph.
steps: Tie in the tail and rib.
Dub a tapered body and rib it.
Tie in the wing case, dub the thorax, pull the case over and fold back the tips as legs.
Whip finish.

new.name: Amy's Ant
new.description: A big foam terrestrial: foam back over a chenille body, rubber legs, an elk hair wing and a foam head.
new.fishing_tips: A hopper/cricket/stonefly suggestion; also a good indicator dry.
steps: Wrap a chenille body.
Tie the foam over the top in segments.
Add the wing and legs at the front.
Fold the foam forward into a head and whip finish.

new.name: Comparadun
new.description: A hackleless dun with a 180° deer hair fan wing and split tails: floats low and lands like a natural.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it during mayfly hatches on flat water.
steps: Tie in a deer hair wing facing forward.
Tie in split tails.
Dub the body, then build dubbing in front of the wing to stand it up in a fan.
Whip finish.

new.name: Nuke Egg
new.description: A two-part yarn egg: a bright core inside a translucent veil, so it glows like a real egg.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it near spawning fish.
steps: Tie a small yarn core and trim it into a ball.
Tie a thin veil of translucent yarn in front, pull it back over the core.
Tie it down behind and trim; whip finish at the eye.

new.name: Quasimodo Pheasant Tail
new.description: A pheasant tail on a curved hook with an oversized humped thorax and a tungsten bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in fast water.
steps: Add the bead, tie in a pheasant tail tail and body, rib it.
Build a big humped peacock thorax.
Pull the wing case over and whip finish.

new.name: Pheasant Tail Soft Hackle
new.description: A pheasant tail body ribbed with wire, a peacock thorax and a partridge hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it through riffles during hatches.
steps: Wrap a pheasant tail body and rib it.
Wrap a small peacock thorax.
Wind one or two turns of partridge, whip finish.

new.name: Hare's Ear Soft Hackle
new.description: A rough hare's ear body ribbed with gold and a partridge hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it or dead-drift it in riffles.
steps: Dub a rough body and rib it.
Wind a sparse partridge hackle.
Whip finish.

new.name: Crackleback
new.description: A palmered fly with a yellow body and peacock herl pulled over the back, fished dry, wet or twitched.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the surface, then pull it under and retrieve.
steps: Tie in peacock herl and the hackle at the bend.
Wrap a yellow body.
Palmer the hackle forward and pull the herl over the back.
Whip finish.

new.name: Devil Bug
new.description: A simple deer hair bug: a bundle of hair tied at the tail and folded forward over the body, forming the back and head.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it on the surface for bluegills and bass.
steps: Tie a bundle of deer hair at the bend, tips back as a tail.
Wrap an underbody.
Fold the hair forward over the top, tie it down behind the eye, trim to a head.
